text.p: Argentine steel company Siderca will invest more than $200 million over the next three years to boost output, the firm's president wrote in a newspaper supplement Tuesday.
"In this way, the conditions will be achieved to meet the growing demands of the most important international clients," Paolo Roca wrote in the El Cronista supplement.
"During 1997 the objective will be the integration and consolidation of our world operations with our affiliates Tamsa (Tubos de Acero de Mexico SA ) in Mexico and Dalmine (SpA) in Italy."

Rocca said Argentine demand for industrial steel tube segments was recovering strongly. The company also hopes for growth from South American energy pipeline projects and oil company investment in drilling.
"For these reasons we see our perspectives for 1997 with optimism," Rocca said.
Siderca delivered 700,000 tonnes of steel products in 1995/96.
